Hurricane Trudy gains strength near Mexico’s coast, but is expected to weaken by Sunday

Reuters

18 October, 2026 05:00 am IST

Follow Us :

MEXICO CITY, Oct 17 (Reuters) – Hurricane Trudy gained some strength as it moved toward Mexico’s western coast on Saturday, with forecasters warning it could strengthen a little more overnight before beginning to weaken on Sunday.

The US National Hurricane Center said Trudy was about 115 miles (180 km) south-southwest of Manzanillo on Saturday afternoon, with maximum sustained winds of 100 mph (155 kph).

The hurricane was moving at about 10 mph (17 kph) and was forecast to approach the southwestern and west-central Mexican coast and pass near the coast overnight into Sunday.

Show Full Article

Hurricane conditions are expected in the warning area on Saturday night, while tropical storm conditions are expected to spread across the region on Saturday afternoon and evening, the NHC said. Hurricane conditions are also possible in areas under a hurricane watch.

Trudy is forecast to bring 4 to 8 inches (10 to 20 cm) of rain, with higher totals of around 12 inches, across parts of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco through the weekend, raising the risk of life-threatening flooding and landslides, especially in steep terrain, according to the NHC.

Outer rain bands could produce 2 to 4 inches of rain, with isolated totals of around 6 inches, in Guerrero and Nayarit, where localized flash flooding is possible, the center said.

The NHC also warned of dangerous storm surge accompanied by damaging waves in areas exposed to onshore winds.

Swells generated by Trudy were already affecting parts of Mexico’s southwestern coast and are expected to spread northward toward the country’s west-central coast through the weekend, creating life-threatening surf and rip current conditions, the NHC said.

Mexico’s national water agency, CONAGUA, has officially classified Trudy as a Category 2 hurricane.

(Reporting by Stefanie Eschenbacher and Adriana Barrera. Editing by Mark Potter and Franklin Paul)

18 October, 2026 02:30 am IST

Oct 17 (Reuters) – A Lebanese military delegation will present Beirut’s demands for an end to Israeli attacks in Lebanon at a trilateral meeting in Tampa, Florida, on October 20, the Lebanese presidency said in a post on X on Saturday.

Lebanon and Israel have held a number of direct talks in recent months, aimed at ending hostilities since a new war erupted on March 2 between Israel and the Lebanese armed group Hezbollah, triggered by the wider regional conflict.

Under a deal reached through US-brokered Israel-Lebanon talks, Beirut vowed to disarm Hezbollah, which would in turn lead to Israeli troops gradually withdrawing from Lebanon. But Hezbollah has refused to disarm as long as Israeli forces remain on Lebanese land, and Israel has continued striking southern Lebanon.

Ukrainian foreign minister says Russian-held town is a ‘death trap’ with starving residents

Reuters

18 October, 2026 01:00 am IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

Oct 17 (Reuters) – Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on Saturday that Russian occupying forces were turning the Ukrainian town of Oleshky into a “death trap” gripped by starvation, and urged international organisations to help evacuate its residents.

Sybiha made his comments on X a day after Russian President Vladimir Putin pledged, in a conversation with Pope Leo, to cooperate in delivering vital supplies into the town in southern Ukraine’s Kherson region.

“Russians are trying to turn the Ukrainian town of Oleshky into a death trap. The hospital has run out of medicine. Dozens of bodies lie in the streets or in homes, as Russians forbid residents from burying them,” Sybiha wrote.

Show Full Article

“Families are starving, surviving on leftover garden vegetables, preserves and even snails … Ukraine has repeatedly called for safe evacuation and international humanitarian access. These appeals cannot remain unanswered.”

The Kremlin acknowledged in September that Oleshky had critical problems with food and medical supplies but said Russia’s military was working to resolve them. Ukraine’s military has twice used drones to deliver food and medicine to the town.

Sybiha urged the United Nations, the International Committee of the Red Cross and other organisations to “secure safe evacuation corridors and immediate humanitarian access.”

Oleshky lies on the east side of the Dnipro River in Kherson region, which Russian forces mostly occupied soon after the 2022 invasion. A Ukrainian counteroffensive later recaptured large chunks of territory, including the city of Kherson.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy described the situation in Oleshky this week as “genocide.”

Oleshky had a pre-war population of 24,000 people and is now home to around 1,700 residents, including 47 children, according to Danielle Bell, head of the United Nations Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine.

Local prosecutors said on Saturday Russian forces dropped aerial bombs on the city of Kherson, on the opposite bank of the Dnipro from Oleshky, killing an ambulance driver and wounding 40 people.

(Reporting by Ron Popeski;Editing by Rod Nickel)

Italian police clash with protesters in Milan and Bologna

Reuters

18 October, 2026 12:00 am IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

MILAN, Oct 17 (Reuters) – Police fired tear gas on Saturday after coming under attack from protesters throwing stones in the square in front of Milan’s Gothic cathedral, Italian media reported, while there were also clashes in the city of Bologna following protests over the cost of living.

Police in Bologna used a water cannon to try to disperse crowds and made seven arrests after the protest became violent, the ANSA news agency reported.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, facing an election next year, condemned the violence.

Show Full Article

“Demonstrating is a right. Turning our cities into battlegrounds is not,” she said on X.

In Milan, police in riot gear also tried to clear hooded protesters from the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, the luxury shopping arcade on one side of the cathedral square, as groups broke away from the cost-of-living protest.

Shops pulled down their shutters and tourists fled the central area. The central Duomo (Cathedral) metro station was closed during the clashes in which several people were reported injured, and arrests were made, according to the Italian media reports.

The clashes echoed the violence in neighbouring France, where tens of thousands of people, angered by rising costs and declining public services, took to the streets on Saturday in some of the country’s most violent protests in years.

(Writing by Keith Weir. Editing by Mark Potter and Rod Nickel)
